returns a pseudo-random byte in A by mixing the low and high bytes of CIA1 timer A and CIA2 timers A and B, which count freely, so the value depends on when it is called; called by cave set-up, the amoeba, the fireflies and the sound effects
fills colour RAM $D800-$D827 with colour 9, then fills every page of $D800 up to $DBFF from offset Y with the colour in A; the cave set-up calls it with Y=$28 so the status row keeps colour 9
copies every second byte of the 40-character status row at $0C00 (the 20 tile codes; each tile is a code and code+$34) into the save buffer at $9862

draws the 20-code text line at (zpp_46) into the status row at $0C00 as pairs of characters (code, code+$34), turning code $01 into a space; also sets the colour of columns 2-5 and 14-17 to 7 or 1 depending on two of the line's codes
returns the four direction bits of joystick port 1 ($DC01) in A, low bits, 0 = pressed
returns the four direction bits of joystick port 2 ($DC00) in A, low bits, 0 = pressed

reads the fire button into zpa_B8 (bit 4, 0 = pressed), from port 2 when the second-joystick flag zpa_A4 and the player flag are both set and otherwise port 1; entered at $6F03 with the mask already in A
masks the keyboard port with zpa_A4 and, when that is non-zero, reads port A at $DC00, otherwise port B at $DC01, then keeps bit 4, the fire button, in zpa_B8
screen codes of the title screen line BY PETER LIEPA, 20 codes in the game's own alphabet (code + $20 is the ASCII letter, $20 is a space, $10-$19 are the digits)
screen codes of the line WITH CHRIS GREY
screen codes of the menu line 1 PLAYER 1 JOYSTICK; the digits are rewritten by the F3 key
screen codes of the line PLYR 1 ... PLYR 2 used for the two-player score line
screen codes of the line 000000 LAST 000000
screen codes of the line 000000 HIGH 000000 followed by G A M E / O V E R (spaced capitals)
screen codes of the in-game status line PLAYER 1-, 3 MEN, A/0 cave and level, OUT OF TIME and BONUS LIFE messages
screen codes of the menu line CAVE: A LEVEL: 1
screen codes SPACEBAR TO RESUME shown while the game is paused
screen codes PRESS BUTTON TO PLAY
draws object X's 2x2 character tile at (zpp_36): the first character is object_tile_table[X], then +1, +$10, +$11 on the next row (offset $50); the 40-tile cave is drawn as 80 characters wide
finds the 3-byte entry at $53B0 whose first byte equals Y (the map-neighbour offset) and adds its 16-bit screen offset to the base in zpa_34/35, leaving the tile's character address in zpp_36

stores the object code in A at the map cell (zpp_32),Y and draws its 2x2 tile at the matching place in the 80-character-wide scroll buffer (base from the row zpa_92 and column zpa_91, neighbour offset from Y); returns A unchanged
writes object 0 (space) into the cell at (zpp_32),Y=$29 and redraws it, then continues at the end-of-object handler $81AD
one step of the 16-bit linear random generator in zpa_3E/3F used to scatter objects when a cave is first built
if the neighbouring cell at (zpp_32),Y is not steel wall (object 7) stores the explosion object from zpa_89 there

turns the 3x3 block of map cells centred on the cell below the current one into explosion objects (zpa_89, one less after the middle cell of the current row, because later cells of the pass will be stepped once more in the same pass), skipping steel wall; then plays the explosion sound; used when a falling rock or diamond lands on a creature or on Rockford
handler for object $04, the closed exit, which looks like steel wall; once the quota flag zpa_90 is set it replaces the exit with object $05, the open flashing exit

turns the 3x3 block of map cells centred on the current cell into explosion objects (zpa_89 for the cells before the centre in scan order and for the centre, one less after it), skipping steel wall; falls into the explosion sound at $7129
sets the sound lockout a_9811 to $50, silences voice 2 and loads the seven SID voice 2 registers from the table at $713D, a noise burst
SID voice 2 settings for the explosion: frequency $1432, pulse width $000F, control $81 (noise, gate on), attack/decay $1B, sustain/release $00

offsets from the map pointer of the neighbour cell in each of four directions, 0 = left, 1 = up, 2 = right, 3 = down; the pointer sits at the top-left of the 3x3 block, so the current cell is at offset $29
offsets of the neighbour cell one turn anticlockwise (to the left of the way it faces) from each of the four directions
leaves X unchanged unless the cell at (zpp_32),Y holds object $38-$3A, then sets X to 0
tests the four neighbouring cells with is_rockford_here and returns with Z set (X=0) if one holds an object $38-$3A

handler for objects $08-$0B, a firefly facing left, up, right or down; explodes (object $1C) when Rockford is adjacent, otherwise moves into the empty cell on its left-hand side and turns that way, else moves straight on, else turns clockwise in place; the cell it enters gets the matching object $0C-$0F, which the end-of-object remap turns back to $08-$0B
counts a sound request in a_980D and builds the diamond-landing note for voice 1 in the buffer at $987D: the four bytes at diamond_sound_data and a random pitch
voice 1 register values for the rock thud: noise, frequency $0932, pulse width $0007, control $81, attack/decay $00, sustain/release $F0
counts a sound request in a_980D and copies the seven thud register values from sid_thud_regs into the voice 1 buffer at $987D
returns X=1 when the object in A is a boulder ($10), a diamond ($14) or a brick wall ($02), the things a rock can roll off sideways, and X=0 for anything else; Z is clear when X=1
sets Z and puts the explosion start code in zpa_89 when the cell at (zpp_32),Y holds an unmoved firefly ($08-$0B, code $1C) or butterfly ($30-$33, code $21); otherwise Z is clear

handler for objects $30-$33, a butterfly; explodes into diamonds (code $21) when Rockford is adjacent, otherwise moves into the neighbour cell in its direction if that is empty and turns clockwise, else sidesteps into the cell one turn anticlockwise keeping its direction, else turns clockwise in place; the cell it enters gets the moved object $34-$37
stores object $15, a diamond at rest that has been handled this pass, in the current cell and ends the handler

handler for object $16, a falling diamond; moves down as $17 while the cell below is empty; on the magic wall (object 3, active) it comes out two cells lower as a falling boulder ($13); lands on Rockford or a creature as an explosion centred below; otherwise rolls off a boulder, diamond or brick wall into an empty side cell whose cell below is empty too, or stays as $15

handler for object $14, a diamond at rest; starts falling (object $17 in the cell below, with the diamond sound) when that cell is empty, rolls into the empty cell to its left or right, when the cell below that one is empty too, if it rests on a boulder, a diamond or a brick wall ($02, not steel or magic wall), otherwise stays
the four cell offsets 1 (up), $28 (left), $2A (right), $51 (down) used when the amoeba picks a direction

handler for objects $3A and $3B, the amoeba; counts itself in a_9802; once the count of the previous pass reached 200 it turns to a boulder, when it had no room to grow it turns to a diamond; otherwise looks for an empty or dirt neighbour (flag zpf_42) and with a random chance set by the rate in zpa_9A grows into one
adds one man to zpa_5C (never above 9) and starts the glisten effect by setting zpa_A8 to $80
compares the thousands and hundreds digits of the score with their values before the add (zpa_A9, zpa_AA) and calls add_life when the score has crossed a multiple of 500

saves the thousands and hundreds digits of the score, adds the six decimal digits at zpf_4E to the score digits at zpf_5F, writes them as characters to the status line at $9848 and checks for the bonus life
voice 3 register values for the time and quota sound: frequency $2F32.., control $81, attack/decay $19, sustain/release $01
sets zpa_D8, which makes the sound routine play the voice 3 effect for $21 frames

when the first two time digits are zero and the last is not, beeps on voice 2 with a pitch that rises as the last digit falls (high byte $27 minus the digit); when all three are zero sets zpa_97 to 2, the cave-over state that the exit, the restart key and running out of time all use; the beep is skipped while the sound lockout a_9811 is not zero
subtracts one from the three-digit decimal time left in zpa_AB-AD, writes the digits to the status line at $9844 and runs the low-time check
once a second runs time_down_one, adds one to the seconds counter zpa_AF and sets the amoeba growth mask zpa_9A to $0F when the counter equals the cave header byte at $2401
counts down the start-of-cave delay zpa_95 each second; at zero plays the voice 3 effect, ends the intro (zpa_93 = 0) and starts play (zpa_94 = 1)
draws the status line from the buffer at $983A
counts frames in zpa_AE; once every 60 frames, unless paused, runs the second tick or the intro countdown
adds one to the two-digit decimal diamonds-collected counter at zpf_B0 and writes the digits to $9841
writes the two digits of zpf_B2, the diamonds needed, to $983B as characters
writes the digits of zpf_52, the value of a diamond, to $983E as characters

when diamonds collected equals diamonds needed sets the quota flag zpa_90, makes the later-diamond value (zpf_B4) the one in use, writes the status line, starts the voice 3 effect and sets the white flash zpa_A5 to 6
voice 1 register values for the diamond pickup chime: frequency $1478, pulse width $0007, control $11, attack/decay $00, sustain/release $F0

five bytes ($07, $00, $11, $00, $F0) for the diamond pick-up sound, read by the routine at $71C5, which uses only the first four, and, through the register table at $7522, by pick_up_diamond, which reads all five
copies the chime values into the voice 1 buffer, adds the diamond's value to the score, counts it and checks the quota, then counts the move in zpa_B7
on one call in four counts the move in zpa_B7, plays the thud and stores object $11, a boulder handled this pass, in the cell beyond; this is the chance that Rockford manages to push a boulder

examines the cell at (zpp_32),Y that Rockford wants to enter: space sets the walk sound and counts the move, dirt sets the dig sound and counts the move, a diamond is picked up, the open exit sets zpa_97 to 2 and zpa_9F to 1, a boulder is pushed sideways when the cell beyond is empty; leaves zpa_B7 non-zero when the move succeeds

runs try_enter_cell; on success with the fire button not pressed puts Rockford ($39) in the new cell and space in the old one; with fire pressed only the new cell is cleared (the object is taken without moving)

moves Rockford one cell for the joystick bits in A (down $0D, up $0E, right below 8, left 8 to $0B), keeping the scroll locked at the edges, and updates his column zpa_44 or row zpa_45; zpa_98 records the way he faces

handler for objects $38-$3A, Rockford; takes the joystick bits from the demo script (zpa_8B) when zpa_A2 is set, otherwise from joystick 1 or, for player 2 with two joysticks, joystick 2, then calls rockford_move
pairs of (current, next) explosion codes: $1F becomes space, $1E to $1F, $1D to $1E, $1C to $1D, $1B to $1C; $24 becomes a diamond ($14), $23 to $24, $22 to $23, $21 to $22, $20 to $21
pairs of (current code, next code) for the explosion's stages, so that each stage turns into the next and the last into a space or a diamond
pairs of (current, next) codes for Rockford's arrival: $28 becomes Rockford ($38), $27 to $28, $26 to $27, $25 to $26
the last pairs of the arrival table: Rockford's arrival stages $28 down to $25 turn into the next stage and the last becomes Rockford ($38)
the last bytes of the arrival code table at $7663: stages $27 to $25 for Rockford's appearance
handler for objects $1B-$24; looks up the next code in the table at $764F and stores it, so a creature's explosion fades to space and a butterfly's to a diamond
handler for objects $26-$28; once the intro delay zpa_95 has run out steps the arrival sequence to the next code in the table at $7663
draws tile $2E, a blank, at the current tile position; used to make the entrance flash
works out the screen position of the current cell and draws the blank tile there
handler for objects $05 (the open exit) and $25 (the entrance); on alternate calls it draws the blank tile, and when the object is $25 and the intro delay has ended hands over to the arrival sequence

handler for object $10, a boulder at rest; starts falling (object $13 in the cell below, with the thud) when that cell is empty; otherwise, when it rests on a boulder, a diamond or a brick wall ($02), rolls left, or failing that right, into an empty cell whose cell below is empty too
stores object $11, a boulder at rest that has been handled, in the current cell

handler for object $12, a falling boulder; keeps falling through empty space, lands on Rockford or a creature as an explosion centred below, turns a diamond-making magic wall pass into a diamond ($17) two cells lower, otherwise rolls off or comes to rest as $11
writes zero to the eight sparkle bytes at $3300, $3304, $3308, $330C, $3380, $3384, $3388, $338C
while the glisten counter zpa_A8 runs, fills the sparkle bytes at $3300-$338C with random values (clearing them on the last step) so the dug-out cells shimmer
rotates the eight bytes at $2000 up by one, wrapping the first to the last
vertical scroll speed table, three bytes per entry: Rockford's window row, then the speed
$C0, the low byte of the first scroll speed constant for the rows
$FF, the high byte of the same constant, so the value is -64 as a 16-bit number
horizontal scroll speed table, three bytes per entry: Rockford's window column, then the speed
$C0, the low byte of the first scroll speed constant for the columns
$FF, the upper half of the column constant that pairs with the $C0 at $7840 (the two make -64)

when both horizontal phases zpa_E1 and zpa_E2 are zero recomputes Rockford's column within the window (zpa_E6), then when both vertical phases are zero his row (zpa_E5), from his map column zpa_44 and row zpa_45 and the scroll positions zpa_E8 and zpa_EC

second entry of the scroll-window routine: sets the target window row zpa_E6 to the player's row (zpa_44) minus half the vertical scroll amount in zpa_E8, then, only when no scroll is running (zpa_E3 and zpa_E4 are zero), falls through to the column target
sets the target window column zpa_E5 to the player's column (zpa_45) minus half the horizontal scroll amount in zpa_EC
the four VIC control register 2 values $15, $13, $11, $17 for the horizontal fine scroll phases
the four VIC control register 1 values $17, $15, $13, $11 for the vertical fine scroll phases

adds the vertical speed zpa_ED/EE to the 16-bit scroll position zpa_EB/EC, takes the fine phase zpa_E3 from bits 7 and 6 of the low byte zpa_EB, writes the matching vertical scroll value to zpa_54, and moves the screen base zpa_D6/D7 by one character row ($50 characters of the 80-wide buffer) when the phase goes from 0 to 1 or back; stops early on odd frames when aligned

the same for the horizontal direction: speed zpa_E9/EA, position zpa_E7/E8, phase zpa_E1, VIC scroll value into zpa_56 (with the 40-column bit set in the intermission caves when the intro has ended), screen base zpa_D6/D7 moved by one character
sets the scroll speeds to zero when the position reaches the cave's left or top edge, or $15 (vertical) or $2A (horizontal) in the high byte at the right or bottom edge
sets the vertical speed to +$0040 when Rockford's window row zpa_E5 is $0B or more and to -$0040 when it is below 5
sets the horizontal speed to +$0040 when Rockford's window column zpa_E6 is $11 or more and to -$0040 when it is below 3
looks up the scroll speeds in the vertical table at $7833 (row, speed low, speed high) and the horizontal table at $783F by Rockford's window row and column, and calls the two edge speed routines
unless play is held, updates Rockford's window position, the scroll speeds and edge stops, and takes the horizontal and vertical steps
adds one to the map pointer zpp_32/33
sets the map pointer zpp_32/33 to $0827, or $084F when Z is clear; the cell the update pass handles is at pointer + $29
fills the 22 pairs of rows of the 80-character-wide scroll buffer, 160 characters per entry of the row table at $53DA, with character $7C
sets up the row pointers from the screen base zpa_D6/D7, then puts the character $7C at random places on every row of the scroll buffer, used to wipe the cave away at the end
writes $4A into the 259 bytes at $4DC3-$4EC2 and $4000-$4002, the edges of the scroll buffer
draws the cave onto the covered screen by picking a random column in each of the 22 rows and drawing that cell, $45 passes; the opening reveal of a cave

while the intro flag zpa_BD is set plays a random tick on voice 2 one frame in three (a counter at a_980B runs 1, 2, 3: the tick starts on 1 and the gate closes on 3) and, every frame, rotates the eight bytes at $33E0 so the cover character animates
calls the random reveal, then draws every cell of the cave in order into the scroll buffer and fills the buffer edges

builds Rockford's character frame in $3260/$32E0 from the tables at $64E8 (facing left) or $65E8 (right) for the moving cases; when standing still (zpa_8B = $0F, X = frame step) the blink is the 8 bytes at $63E8 drawn into the head character $3260 when zpa_BF is set (one chance in four, chosen at random), and the foot-tap is the 8 bytes at $6468 drawn into the feet character $32E0 while zpa_BE is set (toggled with one chance in sixteen)

builds the animated characters of the current phase zpa_C0 into the character set: the diamond (char $48 at $3240) and Rockford always, and the firefly (bit 0 of the mask zpf_FF, char $64 at $3320), butterfly (bit 1, char $20 at $3100) and amoeba (bit 2, char $40 at $3200) sets only when the cave uses them
while the flash counter zpa_A5 runs turns the background and border colours white, and black when it ends

once a frame plays what the game asked for: the low-time and quota effect on voice 3 and the amoeba hum, the buffered voice 1 notes from $987D, the step and dig notes on voice 2 and the end-of-time tone; does nothing when paused
copies eight bytes from $3270 into four places in the character set at $3110, $3118, $3190 and $3198
while the magic wall is active plays a random note on voice 3 on alternate frames and cycles eight bytes from $3360 into the character set at $3110-$31A0, animating the wall
runs the magic wall animation while it is active (zpa_8D = 1) and ends it at state 2
advances the animation phase zpa_C0 by 8 modulo $40, builds the new frames and runs the magic wall animation
while the magic wall is active and the game is not paused counts frames in zpa_8E and seconds in zpa_8F, and when the seconds equal the cave header byte at $2401 sets zpa_8D to 2, the wall expired

the once-per-frame job started from the interrupt when zpa_A7 is zero: flash, intro effects, magic wall timer, clock, sound, scrolling, then on every second frame the screen copy routine, on the others it swaps the double-buffer flag

256 bytes of code that are copied to $9E00 at start and run from there: they work out the scroll buffer and screen addresses for the current screen base zpa_D6/D7 and copy rows of the scroll buffer into the screen; the unrolled loads show $5000 and $0C50 because the real operands are patched in at $9E00
the second 256-byte block of code copied to $9F00: the remainder of the screen copy routine, ending with a call to animation_step and to sparkle_step while the glisten counter runs

makes one random cell of the starting cave: takes a random byte with the generator in zpa_3E/3F, picks space, boulder, diamond or dirt by the four thresholds at $241C and the codes at $2418, and stores it in the cell
fills the cave's rows 1 to 21 (21 rows of 40; row 0 is left alone) with build_cave_cell
per-level delay counts loaded into zpa_9C, 12, 6, 3, 1 and 0
busy-waits for zpa_9C times a short loop; used to slow a pass on the easy levels
writes 8 and then 0 to the control register of SID voice 1 ($D404), so the gate closes
the same for voice 2 ($D40B)
the same for voice 3 ($D412)
silences the three voices and sets the SID volume to $4F
a busy loop of about 128 passes of 256 for timing pauses
four times delay_short
waits about the same time, or leaves at once when the RUN/STOP key flag zpa_FC is $EF
shows the pause text on the status line and flashes it until the space-bar flag zpa_FC says to carry on
handles the keyboard flags: SPACE ($EF in zpa_FC) pauses the game, RUN/STOP ($7F) ends the cave in progress (zpa_97 = 2), and F1 ($EF in zpa_FB) restarts the whole program at $8E6A

after the update pass records whether the amoeba found room to grow (zpf_42 into zpa_43), clearing the growth flag zpa_8C when it had room before and none now, and copies the amoeba count a_9802 to a_9803
runs read_fire; when Rockford has been in the cave for $10 passes, fire is pressed and a diamond has been collected, sets zpa_97 to 2 so the player can give up the cave

the once-per-frame pass over the cave: walks every cell from row 1, looks the cell's object up in the table of handlers at $5F68 and jumps to the handler when it has one; the handlers end at $81AD, which applies the remap table at $5EE8, turning the 'handled' object codes back into their normal ones, and goes on to the next cell

applies the remap table at $5EE8 to the cell just handled, then advances to the next cell and column and, after each row, delays on the easy levels; at the end of the last row does the keyboard checks
the weights 0, 0, 1 added by the decimal conversion
converts the count in zpa_C6 into three decimal digits in zpf_C3-C5 by adding the weights at $81D6 with carry, counting zpa_C6 down

the operand of the branch at $81FB in binary_to_decimal, which repeats the decimal conversion loop at $81E6 until the count in zpa_C6 reaches zero; the byte just before the cave order table at $81FE, which next_cave reads as data at $8BDC (the table's base, indexed by twice the cave number)
two bytes per cave number, giving the cave that follows each one and the flag whether it is an intermission; the value $15 ends a round and raises the level

when the cave number zpa_5D has changed copies the $F0-byte description of the cave (at $582E plus the offset in the table at $5804) into $2400, then takes the random seed for the level, sets the two multicolour registers from $2413/$2414 and fills colour RAM from $2415

clears the cave's play variables; sets the delay for the level, the time ($240E+level), the diamonds needed and the value of a diamond, the three time digits, the intro delay zpa_95 and the scroll limits; sets the amoeba rate zpa_9A to $7F and the object mask zpf_FF from the table at $8740
draws the GAME OVER line at $6F8C and waits
waits about 10 seconds for the fire button or a key press; returns early when fire is seen
shows the last and high score lines for about 5 seconds, flashing, until fire is pressed
shows the cave and level line at the start of a cave and awards the glisten effect
when the diamond count reaches the quota stops play, shows the bonus and score lines, then wipes the cave (scatter) and awaits fire; when the game is over shows the game over text
the map-screen row start addresses, $0800 plus $28 per row, 24 entries, words from $0800 to $0B98
the rest of the table of 40 screen-row start addresses, as little-endian words from $0850 in steps of $28: the map row addresses drawn by the routine at $8436
turns the row zpa_DC and column zpa_DB of a cave-description object into the address zpa_3A/3B in the map
stores the object in zpa_DA in the map cell addressed by the row and column of the current cave description object
the 16-bit steps for the eight directions of cave-description lines
the rest of the eight direction steps, 16-bit words such as -1, 1, -40 and 40 for the neighbours of a map cell, read by the line routine at $8464
stores the object zpa_DA in zpa_C8 cells along the direction in A starting at the cell addressed by zpa_3A/3B
draws a line object of the cave description: a start cell, a length and a direction
fills a rectangle of width zpa_DD and height zpa_DF with object zpa_DA
draws the filled rectangle, then the object zpa_E0 inside it
draws the four sides of a rectangle with object zpa_DA
advances Y over the bytes of the current cave description object
adds two to the byte index in Y and runs the routine at $8507 that adds three more and stores it in zpa_CB, so one cave-object record is stepped over
adds one to Y and then steps over the rest of the record through the routine at $850D

walks the cave description list from $2420: each record starts with a code (top two bits: 00 single point, 40 line, 80 filled rectangle with an inner fill, C0 outline rectangle; low six bits the object); stops at the end byte $FF; for object $25 (the entrance) it also records Rockford's column zpa_44 and row zpa_45
writes the two player-number characters of the status line at $0B70/$0B84
draws a steel wall ($07) frame around the 40 by 22 cave

builds the title and menu screen into the map at $0828 and the lines of text at $0AF8-$0B98 from the tables at $6F14-$7004 (on one path the lines at $0B20 and $0B48 instead come from the score buffers at $9812 and $9826) and the map part from the title templates at $66E8-$68E7
the table of SID frequency words the title music reads (two bytes per note from this address, so notes 0-9 overlap the code above); the entries from $86DE are 49 notes rising from $02DC to $2DC0
the high byte of each frequency word in the table at $86CA, read at the same index as the low byte
16-bit offsets $02DC, $030A, ... used to locate each cave's description
one byte per cave number, 1 to 20, loaded into zpf_FF: bit 0 the cave has fireflies, bit 1 butterflies, bit 2 the amoeba; the other creatures' animated characters are then not rebuilt each frame
on every other call plays the next pair of notes of the title tune on voices 1 and 2, with a short envelope that is steepened as the step counter a_980C changes
ORs the eight bytes at $2030 and $2038 with $2000 into $2048 and $2050, building the cycling colour characters
once per frame at the title screen advances the title animation: every fourth frame rotates the colour table, rebuilds the colour characters and plays the next music step

decodes the F3 key at the title (zpa_FB = $DF): cycles zpa_D0 through one player, two players with one joystick and two players with two joysticks, updates the player and joystick flags zpa_9E and zpa_A4 and redraws the menu line

at the title reads joystick 1: left and right choose the cave (zpa_5D in steps of four from A: A, E, I, M) and up and down the level (zpa_5E, 1 to 5), and redraws the letter and digit characters on the menu line at $0BA6 and $0BBA
the title menu loop: handles the F3 and key flags, joystick choices and the fire button, until play is started (b_CD set)

copies the eight colour bytes at $2058 to $2000, sets cave 1 and the demo flag, runs the menu loop once, then sets the VIC register tables zpa_54-5B from $89A4, resets the key flags and builds the menu lines
the border, background and extra background colours for the title screen, written to $D020-$D024
eight bytes loaded into zpa_54-5B for the in-game screen: VIC control and memory registers for the two raster regions, and the raster lines
the same eight bytes for the title screen
clears the map area, sets the VIC to charset $2000, paints the screen with colour 9, waits for the interrupt to set zpa_CF and clears the music and sound state

the game's interrupt: alternates between the two screen regions by writing the VIC registers from the tables at zpa_54-5B, scans the keyboard rows for F1, F3, SPACE and RUN/STOP with a two-read debounce into zpa_FB-FE, then at the title runs title_step and in play runs frame_update
if joystick 1 is moved or fired clears the debounced key flags and skips the keyboard handling in this interrupt

loads the cave description, fills the cave with random objects, draws the steel border, builds the cave from its description, sets the play variables, zeroes the scroll speeds and draws the whole cave
clears the score and the extra-life and game-over flags, sets three men and copies the first player's state into the two player save areas

takes a man from the current player, saves that player's state and, in a two-player game, switches to the other player when they still have men; sets the game-over flag zpa_A0 when nobody has any left
plays one rising run of notes on voice 3 for the end-of-cave bonus count
compares the six score digits with the high score digits and, when the score is higher, copies it over the high score
writes the two players' last scores and the high scores into the score lines at $9813-$9833 as characters
takes the next cave number from the order table at $81FE; at the end of a round ($15) goes back to cave A and raises the level, up to level 5
counts the time left into the score one second at a time, adding level plus one points per second with a blip each, then goes on to the next cave
updates the high score and takes a man or switches player; sets the cave to the title when the game is over

holds play; after a finished cave runs the time bonus, after an intermission goes to the next cave, otherwise runs end_player_turn; then rewrites the status characters for the player, men, cave and level
the cave's main loop: runs update_pass again and again until a cave-ending state is set in zpa_97, then silences the sound, runs the end-of-cave actions and waits for the glisten effect to finish

plays the demonstration: reads the move script at $5EA8, a byte at a time with the direction in the low four bits and, when that is not zero, a repeat count in the high four bits, runs one update pass per repeat and ends when the fire button is pressed
copies the LAST and HIGH score text lines from $6F64 and $6F78 into $9812 and $9826, blanks the line at $983A and sets $983D to $3C

copies the character set and the tables from where the program file holds them to where the VIC reads them ($5000-$53FF to $2000-$23FF, $5FE8-$62E7 to $3000-$33FF, and the frame tables at $6BE8-$6DA8 and $68E8-$6AA8 into $3840-$3E80), clears the animation areas, sets the sprite pointers to $DE and puts the seven sprites in place

silences the sound and resets the key flags, scroll phases, cave variables and counters; the first time through also sets the border colours, the score digits and the sprite tables and runs init_score_lines and init_graphics
sets the screen buffer, loads the VIC table from $899C, switches on the raster interrupt at line $28 and points the interrupt vector at $8A0C

the program's real start, the target of the loader's jump and also of the RESTORE key's NMI vector: sets up the CIA timers that feed the random generator, the NMI vector, the banking, copies the two screen-copy templates from $7EF0 and $7FF0 to $9E00 and $9F00, loads the status line template and runs the title and game loop: with no cave chosen the title screen, otherwise sets up the cave, plays it (or the demo) and ends it
23 bytes after the program that nothing refers to: ASCII ':SK3A' and ':SK4' between bytes $A8 $00 and $85 $00, purpose unknown
screen codes of the word EXIT
the copy of the code at $7EF0, patched at run time: works out the scroll buffer and screen addresses for the current screen base and copies rows of the buffer into the screen
the copy of the code at $7FF0: the rest of the screen copy, ending with animation_step and the sparkle step
